verdict.label: not_comparable
verdict.rationale: Both claims concern all-cause mortality with sulfonylureas versus an active comparator, but the contrasts answer different questions. Side A (PMID 36944118) evaluates second-line SU versus non-SU second-line therapy (DPP4i/TZD) in metformin failures in Scotland (HR 1.03, 0.90-1.17, IV analysis; authors conclude SU 'unlikely to increase CV risk or all-cause mortality'). Side B (PMID 34251086) evaluates first-line SU versus metformin in new users from the UK CPRD, and its selected estimate is further restricted to the normal-weight BMI subgroup (HR 1.18, 0.99-1.42; authors state no increased risk 'among normal-weight patients'). The reference treatment (DPP4i/TZD vs metformin), treatment line/population (second-line metformin failures vs first-line new users), and granularity (overall vs BMI subgroup) all differ, so no sufficiently similar comparable contrast is identifiable from the abstracts. Both sides' extractions were verified against their sources and no material extraction error was found; the obstacle is comparability, not extraction.

source_evidence.quote: A cohort study was performed including people with type 2 diabetes diagnosed in Scotland before 31 December 2017, who failed to reach HbA1c 48 mmol/mol despite metformin monotherapy and initiated second-line pharmacotherapy (SU/DPP4i/TZD) on or after 1 January 2010.

Comparing SU to non-SU (DPP4i/TZD), the hazard ratio (HR) for MACE was 1.00 (95% CI: 0.91-1.09) from the multivariable Cox regression and 1.02 (0.91-1.13) and 1.03 (0.91-1.16) using two different IVs.

Using the UK Clinical Practice Research Datalink, we conducted a cohort study among 13 862 new sulphonylurea users matched on body mass index (BMI) and propensity score, in a 1:1 ratio, to new metformin users between April 1, 1998 and December 31, 2016.

Similar results were observed for all-cause mortality (HR 1.47, 95% CI 1.32-1.62), where an increased risk was observed among obese patients (HR 1.83, 95% CI 1.49-2.25), but not normal-weight patients (HR 1.18, 95% CI 0.99-1.42; P-interaction: 0.006).

diagnostics.notes: Side A's claim (second IV analysis, all-cause death HR 1.03, 0.90-1.17, hedged directional '+') and Side B's claim (normal-weight subgroup, all-cause mortality HR 1.18, 0.99-1.42, explicit_no_difference per the authors' 'but not normal-weight patients' wording) are each faithful to their abstracts. Had the contrasts been aligned, both would point to no increased mortality risk, but the differing comparator (DPP4i/TZD vs metformin), treatment line, population, and overall-vs-subgroup granularity prevent a like-for-like comparison.
